item.title: Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira appreciated by N10 against the dollar in the parallel market on Friday, exchanging at N1,445 per dollar, compared with N1,455 on Thursday. Similarly, the naira strengthened in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), appreciating to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378 per dollar recorded on Thursday. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market improved by N2 to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official market exchange rates narrowed to N69 per dollar from N77 recorded on Thursday. Meanwhile, the value of interbank turnover in the NFEM fell by 54.5 per cent to $106.9 million from $235.04 million recorded on Thursday. The post Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Guinea-Bissau postpones elections to 2028 over inadequate technical, material condition
item.description: Guinea-Bissau’s military rulers have postponed presidential and parliamentary elections scheduled for next week by nearly two years, further delaying the country’s return to civilian rule. Transitional President, Gen. Horta N’Tam, announced in a decree that the elections, initially scheduled for December 6, would now hold on November 26, 2028. The announcement came exactly one year after the military seized power, promising to restore civilian rule within 12 months. In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of preparations for the elections had revealed insufficient “technical, material and financial conditions” to conduct the polls as scheduled. It said the postponement would provide more time to ensure that the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities. The presidency also reaffirmed its commitment to conducting the country’s first local government elections but did not announce a date for the exercise. Gen. N’Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025. The coup occurred three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were expected to be announced. Both Embaló and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory in the election. Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing interest in contesting the elections. Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974. item.title: ECOWAS Speaker warns of levy shortfalls ahead of 2027 budget
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, Memounatou Ibrahima, has warned that rising public debt and mounting pressure on national finances could undermine member states’ ability to remit the Community Levy, urging governments to strengthen compliance ahead of the consideration of the regional body’s 2027 budget. Ibrahima gave the warning on Friday in Abuja during the opening of the 2026 Second Ordinary Session of the ECOWAS Parliament. She said the proposed 2027 budget was being considered at a time when member states were grappling with increasing demands for development financing and growing pressure on public finances. The Speaker urged national parliaments to intensify engagement with their respective governments to ensure regular collection and remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy. She also called on lawmakers to scrutinise budget proposals and ensure that public allocations addressed clearly identified needs and delivered measurable benefits to citizens across the region. She said: “One of the major highlights of our deliberations will be the consideration of the draft Community Budget for the 2027 financial year. “Indeed, persistent economic and financial constraints, characterised by mounting pressure on public finances and the indebtedness of our Member States, with the attendant risks to the remittance of the Community Levy, as well as increasing demands for development financing, require us to exercise particular vigilance and responsibility.” Ibrahima added: “I wish to urge our national parliaments to intensify their advocacy efforts with Member States at the appropriate political level to ensure the collection and systematic remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy.” She stressed that every budget allocation must be justified by its relevance and expected impact, while priority areas should be determined by efficiency, performance and tangible results for the people. The Speaker said the Parliament would also receive country reports and consider findings from oversight missions covering goods in transit, the ECOWAS Mission in The Gambia, regional agricultural projects and the development of a climate-friendly electricity market. She pledged to work with the new President of the ECOWAS Commission, Gen. Birame Diop, and other community institutions to advance regional integration. Ibrahima also referenced the Lungi Declaration, through which regional leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the legislative and oversight functions of the ECOWAS Parliament. She congratulated Cabo Verde’s President, José Maria Neves, on his re-election and called for peaceful elections in The Gambia and Nigeria, whose presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027. In his remarks, Diop warned that terrorism spreading from the Sahel continued to pose a threat to countries in the coastal region. item.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United have activated a one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, keeping him at the club until 2028. According to the BBC, the option prevents overseas clubs from approaching the Portugal international over a pre-contract agreement when the transfer window opens on January 1. Fernandes’ previous contract was due to expire next summer. Fernandes, 32, and United are understood to have agreed to resume talks over a longer-term deal later, with their immediate focus on improving the club’s league position. The midfielder confirmed on Tuesday that contract discussions had been paused. United have been negotiating with Fernandes since the summer. He has turned down two offers, including the club’s initial proposal, but said the priority should be returning to winning ways. “I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games,” he said. Fernandes joined United from Sporting in January 2020 for £47m. He has since made 343 appearances, scoring 115 goals. Last season, he broke the Premier League assists record and won the individual player of the year awards as United finished third. United were open to selling him in the summer of 2025, when Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal made a substantial offer. After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes chose to stay, though he later said it “hurt” that the club had been willing to sell him. The captain has said he remains ambitious to win major honours at United. “My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am,” he said. Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday’s Premier League match against Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus. He scored both goals in United’s 2-2 draw with his former club but missed training on Friday. “We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up,” head coach Mauricio Pochettino said. “We are not going to take any risks.” The post Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Wike’s Imo campaign demand an insult, says RHGN leader
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Deputy National Leader (South-East) of Renewed Hope for Greater Nigeria (RHGN), Mazi Franklin Ngoforo, has described as an insult to the people of Imo State and the South-East a reported request by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to lead President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign in the state. Ngoforo, an indigene of Imo State, said Wike’s reported demand suggested that the state lacked the political capacity and leadership structures to determine its own political direction. He questioned why a political figure from outside Imo would seek to take charge of the president’s re-election campaign in a state with a history of producing prominent national figures and successful entrepreneurs. Ngoforo, in a statement, alleged that Wike’s political ambition reflected a desire to dominate and control political affairs in the South-East rather than build genuine partnerships with the people. He warned against what he described as attempts by outsiders to assume the role of colonial masters over the region’s political space. The RHGN leader maintained that Imo State possessed the political maturity, leadership capacity and grassroots structures to determine its electoral choices without external control. He insisted that no individual could claim ownership of the state’s political destiny. Ngoforo, however, expressed confidence that President Tinubu would secure re-election in Imo State in 2027, citing the mobilisation capacity of RHGN across the state. He said members of the organisation were already engaging communities and voters, taking the Renewed Hope message to the grassroots and building support for the President. item.title: N450bn rice fund: Atiku asks Tinubu, ‘Where are the farmers, where are the mills?’
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain how his administration’s claimed N450 billion investment in rice production is benefiting local farmers, as more than 90 rice mills have reportedly shut down and an importer was allegedly granted concessions to bring in 150,000 metric tonnes of brown rice. Atiku said the developments raised serious questions about the government’s commitment to local rice production, particularly when farmers were struggling with rising production costs and mill operators were reportedly shutting down because of inadequate supplies of locally grown paddy. In a statement on Friday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, accused the Tinubu administration of using impressive spending figures to mask the difficulties confronting the rice industry. “This is the Tinubu government’s familiar trick: announce a fortune, hide the failure, and call anyone who asks for the receipts ungrateful. Nigerians are tired of being manipulated. “Show the farmers who received the money. Show the mills that reopened. Explain the import concession. Until then, the N450 billion claim is propaganda dressed up as a harvest,” he said. Atiku demanded that the government account for the claimed N450 billion intervention, which he said comprised N250 billion for smallholder farmers and N200 billion for a guaranteed minimum price programme. He questioned how much of the money had actually been disbursed, who benefited and what quantities of locally produced rice had been purchased under the programme. “Committed is a convenient word for a campaign. Farmers need to know what was disbursed, who received it, what produce was purchased and what price was paid,” he said. The former vice president also cited reports that more than 90 of Nigeria’s 260 integrated rice mills had shut down amid shortages of locally produced paddy, rising operating costs and competition from cheaper imported rice. “These are livelihoods disappearing: farmers without dependable buyers, workers without jobs and investors watching expensive machinery stand idle. No presidential campaign can wave away that wreckage with a press release,” he said. He said farmers in Kano, Kebbi, Katsina and other parts of the country were already battling insecurity and soaring fertiliser and diesel costs, warning that cheaper imports could further undermine local production and investment. “We built the mills. We grow the grain. We will not accept a future in which Nigerian farmers lose their livelihoods while the government celebrates imports as progress,” he said. item.title: EPL: Arsenal cannot take advantage of Man City’s poor form for granted – Arteta
item.description: Mikel Arteta insisted Friday that Arsenal will not underestimate spluttering Manchester City in Sunday’s crucial clash with their Premier League title rivals. Arteta’s leaders are six points clear of third-placed City heading into the showdown at the Emirates Stadium. City led the table in the opening months of the season before suffering a major dip in recent weeks. Enzo Maresca’s men have only won just in their last seven games in all competitions and are without a victory in their last four league matches. Arteta cannot explain City’s stumble but he has no intention of taking three points for granted against them. “I don’t know, that’s a question for them. All I can say is when I watch them play, a lot of the games they have to win they do more than the opponent, but this is football,” the Arsenal manager told reporters on Friday. “When we play the home games against big teams that becomes crucial in the title challenge, we know how important those games are. But the second part, we’re in November, and we still have long to play. “The challenge is for us, we cannot control what other opponents are going to do.” City boss Maresca has been criticised for his team’s poor form but Arteta is a firm admirer of the Italian, who is in his first season in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. “I know Enzo personally and he’s a phenomenal guy. He lives and breathes football, is very analytical. He is already on the great managerial career already. Everything is super positive,” Arteta said. – Arsenal ‘hunger’ – Arsenal sit top despite also being below their peak form in recent weeks. They were held to draws in their last two games against Newcastle in the Premier League and Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Prior to that, the Gunners eked out three wins by a one-goal margin and suffered an embarrassing League Cup exit at fourth-tier Fleetwood. Arteta believes Arsenal are still rounding into form and he hopes the motivation of a valuable victory against City will spur them on as they chase the high of a second successive title. “Yes, more hunger to do it again. To have those moments again together,” he said. “Everybody puts in unbelievable shifts every week, to analyse the opponent, to breathe the right atmosphere around the boys and to win the game, week in, week out.” City’s dynastic run under Guardiola is an inspiration to Arteta even if they have lost their way lately. “You certainly learn from that. And that inspires you to go to a different level, and that’s the level Manchester City brought to this league, because what they have done is unprecedented,” he said. Arteta revealed David Raya is back in training after missing the Dortmund game with a shoulder injury suffered against Newcastle. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised against Dortmund but Arteta would not reveal if Raya is ready to return to action this weekend. The post EPL: Arsenal cannot take advantage of Man City’s poor form for granted – Arteta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
item.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. President Tinubu was represented at the inauguration by the Vice President, Kashim Shettima. item.title: Fury cleared for Joshua fight after wife retracts schizophrenia claim
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Tyson Fury has been cleared to fight Anthony Joshua after passing the required pre-fight medical checks, following controversy over his wife Paris’s comments about his mental health. According to Sky Sports, British Boxing Board of Control general secretary Robert Smith confirmed Fury had passed his medicals ahead of the heavyweight bout at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium on December 11. “Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning,” Smith said. Paris Fury had said in an initial version of a Netflix documentary that her husband had been diagnosed with schizophrenia. She later clarified that he had never received such a diagnosis and said she had used the word while recalling a conversation from many years ago. “Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis,” she said. Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane. The boxing board had been investigating the comments and could have refused Fury a licence if it found him unfit to fight. Netflix said it had updated the documentary footage following Paris’s clarification. Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane. The documentary explores Fury’s experiences with depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly severe after his 2015 victory over Wladimir Klitschko. Fury has also spoken about drug and alcohol addiction and the difficulties he faced during that period. Paris said she was proud of her husband for speaking openly about his experiences and thanked the public for supporting their family. item.title: Poor-quality hygiene products expose mothers, babies to discomfort – Firm
item.description: Exxon Pharma Nigeria Limited has said that while childbirth is one of the bravest moments in a woman’s life, the days that follow are often the hardest. The company said Nigeria has one of the world’s highest birth rates and has long relied heavily on expensive imported diapers and sanitary pads, as well as cheaper alternatives that often fail when needed most. Against this backdrop, the company said local manufacturing would enable stricter quality control, fresher stock and a more reliable supply, while making prices less vulnerable to foreign exchange fluctuations and shipping delays. In a move aimed at improving access to hygiene products for mothers, babies and young girls, Exxon Pharma Nigeria Limited has launched three products in Nigeria: Wonder Baby Premium Baby Diapers, Wonder Girl Deluxe Maternity Pads and Wonder Girl Sanitary Pads. The company said: “Villa Consumable Ltd. will distribute the products nationwide. Nigeria has one of the world’s highest birth rates and has long relied heavily on expensive imported diapers and pads, or cheaper alternatives that often fail when needed most. Mothers know the story too well: a diaper that leaks overnight, a pad that shifts at school, or a maternity pad that cannot handle postpartum flow. “For a mother, a good diaper means sleep. For a baby, it means comfort. We made Wonder Baby to give both. Childbirth is one of the bravest moments in a woman’s life. item.title: It won’t happen again — Fashola on Peter Obi’s 2023 victory in Lagos
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said the All Progressives Congress was caught off guard by Peter Obi’s victory in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election, insisting the party would not allow a repeat in future elections. Obi, who contested on the platform of the Labour Party, defeated APC candidate Bola Tinubu in his home state, securing a narrow victory that stunned the ruling party. Speaking in an exclusive interview with ARISE News, Fashola admitted that the outcome was unexpected, attributing the party’s surprise to pre-election surveys that did not indicate Lagos was at risk. “We were blindsided. It won’t happen again,” he said. Asked whether the APC had underestimated its opponents by taking Lagos for granted, the former governor rejected the suggestion, explaining that the party’s projections had not identified the state as a major battleground. “Lagos didn’t look like a battleground at the time, not from the numbers,” Fashola said. He added, “We do very scientific surveys, and Lagos didn’t look like a battleground in that sense. So that’s why I say I was blindsided, on reflection.” Fashola, however, said the party recovered from the setback shortly after the presidential election, arguing that subsequent electoral outcomes showed it remained politically strong in the state. “In spite of that setback at the presidential election, we turned it around very quickly,” he said. He also dismissed suggestions that Obi’s victory marked a lasting decline in the APC’s influence in Lagos, saying the party should focus on its record and policies rather than dwell on the past. The former governor spoke amid questions about voter intimidation, ethnic rhetoric and violence during the 2023 elections in Lagos, insisting that political competition should not involve threats, attacks or hate speech. Fashola said politicians could aggressively promote their parties and challenge opponents without resorting to personal attacks or inflammatory rhetoric. “You are entitled to very vigorously and vociferously campaign for your party, as I am doing now, and showing what our record is, without damaging anybody’s name, anybody’s reputation, and without hate speech,” he said. He described democracy as a “non-contact sport”, arguing that parties should compete through ideas, policies and performance rather than intimidation or violence. item.title: Bruno Fernandes misses Man U training ahead of Brentford clash
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes missed the club’s training session on Friday ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford on Saturday, raising concerns over his availability for the encounter. The Portuguese midfielder was absent from the session at Carrington after reportedly feeling slightly unwell. However, his absence was not linked to an injury, with the club opting to rest him as a precaution. According to ESPN, Fernandes is expected to recover in time for Saturday’s fixture at Old Trafford, with manager Mauricio Pochettino hopeful that the midfielder will be available for selection. Fernandes’ absence initially attracted attention after footage released by Manchester United from Friday’s training session showed the team preparing without their captain. The 32 year old remains an important figure in United’s midfield and has recorded six goal involvements in the Premier League this season, scoring four goals and providing two assists. He also comes into the Brentford encounter on the back of an impressive midweek performance, having scored twice in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw against his former club, Sporting. Pochettino will be looking to secure his first victory as United manager after the draw, having previously overseen encouraging performances against Liverpool and Sporting. Brentford, meanwhile, head to Old Trafford in confident mood after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Everton last weekend. Their manager, Keith Andrews, has also expressed admiration for Pochettino, saying he had followed the Argentine’s teams during his own coaching career. Saturday’s meeting presents Pochettino with another opportunity to claim his first win as United manager, with Fernandes’ possible return expected to provide a significant boost to the hosts. item.title: [PHOTOS] Adeleke Sworn In For Second Term As Osun Governor
item.description: Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been sworn in for a second term, beginning another four-year tenure that will run until 2030. Adeleke took the oath of office on Friday, November 27, 2026, at an inauguration ceremony held at the Osogbo Township Stadium. The state Chief Judge administered the oath of office to Deputy Governor Kola Adewusi before swearing in Adeleke. The ceremony was attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who led several dignitaries, including former Osun State Governor Bisi Akande, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and former Senate President Bukola Saraki. The entertainment industry was also represented, with Afrobeats singer Davido, alongside B-Red and Shina Rambo, attending the ceremony to celebrate the governor. Adeleke secured re-election in the August 15, 2026 governorship election on the platform of the Accord Party after defecting from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He polled 511,067 votes to defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who secured 444,815 votes. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term. item.title: Pochettino Eyes Lucky Break At Crisis-Hit Man Utd
item.description: Manchester United are error-prone, leaky at the back, and desperately short of confidence as they face the growing nightmare of a Premier League relegation battle. Talk of the Red Devils going down still appears fanciful, but analysts at Opta say they have a 27 percent chance of dropping into the Championship as they prepare to host impressive Brentford. At the top end of the table, Manchester City’s match at Arsenal appears to be a must-win for Enzo Maresca’s team, who have fallen off the pace after a barren spell.
